result.title: Improving Fake Profile Detection Through Multimodal Learning and Research-Guided Feature Integration
result.summary: Fake accounts continue to undermine online platforms, yet it remains unclear whether multimodal learning offers meaningful improvements over strong metadata baselines or graph-based approaches. In this work, we study bot detection by integrating textual, visual, and account metadata signals on the TwiBot-22 benchmark using a subsample of 30,000 users. We propose a multimodal framework combining pretrained textual (XLM-RoBERTa) and visual (CLIP) embeddings with structured account-level features such as follower counts, posting frequency, and account age, and evaluate multiple modality combinations using CatBoost alongside a Relational Graph Convolutional Network (R-GCN). Results show that metadata alone is highly predictive, while multimodal fusion yields only marginal and largely statistically insignificant gains. The graph-based model underperforms classical variants under the subsampled graph conditions of this study. Overall, our findings suggest that under practical constraints, feature quality and metadata richness matter more than fusion complexity.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作在 TwiBot-22 子样本上结合文本（XLM-RoBERTa）、视觉（CLIP）嵌入与账号元数据，用 CatBoost 与 R-GCN 比较多种模态组合以检测虚假账号，发现元数据本身预测力很强，多模态融合仅带来边际且多不显著的提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是虚假账号分类任务而非推理，视觉嵌入仅作为静态特征输入，不涉及内部推理状态、证据使用或生成过程，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的具体联系。
